data.title: We're Hopeful That Genomictree (KOSDAQ:228760) Will Use Its Cash Wisely
data.description:
Just because a business does not make any money, does not mean that the stock will go down. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. But while the successes are well known, investors should not ignore the very many unprofitable companies that simply burn through all their cash and collapse.

Given this risk, we thought we'd take a look at whether Genomictree (KOSDAQ:228760) shareholders should be worried about its cash burn. In this article, we define cash burn as its annual (negative) free cash flow, which is the amount of money a company spends each year to fund its growth. We'll start by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves in order to calculate its cash runway.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Does Genomictree Have A Long Cash Runway?

A cash runway is defined as the length of time it would take a company to run out of money if it kept spending at its current rate of cash burn. In June 2026, Genomictree had ₩79b in cash, and was debt-free. In the last year, its cash burn was ₩13b. That means it had a cash runway of about 6.3 years as of June 2026. Even though this is but one measure of the company's cash burn, the thought of such a long cash runway warms our bellies in a comforting way. Depicted below, you can see how its cash holdings have changed over time.

Check out our latest analysis for Genomictree

How Well Is Genomictree Growing?

On balance, we think it's mildly positive that Genomictree trimmed its cash burn by 13% over the last twelve months. Unfortunately, however, operating revenue declined by 17% during the period. Considering both these factors, we're not particularly excited by its growth profile. In reality, this article only makes a short study of the company's growth data. You can take a look at how Genomictree has developed its business over time by checking this visualization of its revenue and earnings history.

How Easily Can Genomictree Raise Cash?

While Genomictree seems to be in a fairly good position, it's still worth considering how easily it could raise more cash, even just to fuel faster growth. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. Many companies end up issuing new shares to fund future growth. By comparing a company's annual cash burn to its total market capitalisation, we can estimate roughly how many shares it would have to issue in order to run the company for another year (at the same burn rate).

Since it has a market capitalisation of ₩294b, Genomictree's ₩13b in cash burn equates to about 4.3% of its market value. That's a low proportion, so we figure the company would be able to raise more cash to fund growth, with a little dilution, or even to simply borrow some money.

Is Genomictree's Cash Burn A Worry?

As you can probably tell by now, we're not too worried about Genomictree's cash burn. For example, we think its cash runway suggests that the company is on a good path. While its falling revenue wasn't great, the other factors mentioned in this article more than make up for weakness on that measure. Considering all the factors discussed in this article, we're not overly concerned about the company's cash burn, although we do think shareholders should keep an eye on how it develops.
